title: Raynaud--Faltings reduced fibres for normalized affine base change
statement: Let $D$ be a complete discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] with fraction field $F$. Let $E$ be a finitely generated commutative $D$-algebra, flat as a $D$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Suppose $E_F=E\otimes_D F$ is geometrically normal: for every field extension $F_1/F$, every localization at a prime of $E_F\otimes_F F_1$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then there is a finite field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], with no separability requirement, such that the following holds. Let $R\subset L$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $L$, namely the elements satisfying monic polynomials over $D$, and put $E_R=E\otimes_D R$. Regard $E_R$ as a subring of $E_F\otimes_F L$, and let $C$ be its integral closure inside that ring. Then $C$ is a finite $E_R$-module, is a finitely generated flat $R$-algebra, and is a normal ring. The natural map $C\otimes_R L\to E_F\otimes_F L$ is an isomorphism. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $R$ and every field extension $\Omega/(R/\mathfrak n)$, the ring $(C/\mathfrak nC)\otimes_{R/\mathfrak n}\Omega$ is reduced, meaning it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. The zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0405381, Appendix Theorem A.2 and Remark A.3, printed pp.27-28; geometrically normal generic fibre specialization. Theorem A.6 supplies finite normalization even without excellence; here the base is complete.

proof.text: Fix a uniformizer $\pi$ of $D$. Flatness makes $E\to E[1/\pi]=E_F$ injective: tensor $D\xrightarrow{\pi}D$ with $E$ and iterate. The normal ring $E_F$ is reduced, so $E$ is reduced. If $E=0$, take $L=F$ and $C=0$; all clauses hold. In the remaining steps zero factors and components with empty special fibre are allowed.

source.place: Setup before Tag 09IL; injectivity written out from flatness

proof.text: We record the normalization construction for any complete DVR $V$ with fraction field $K$ and flat finite type $V$-algebra $A$ with normal $A_K$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian and reduced. Its total fraction ring is the finite product $\prod_j\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak a_j)$ over its minimal primes. Completeness makes $V$ Nagata; universal Japaneseness makes each finite type domain $A/\mathfrak a_j$ N-2. Consequently its integral closure in its own fraction field is finite. Integral closure in the finite product is the product of these closures: projection of a monic equation gives one inclusion, and the product of the finitely many monic equations gives the other. This product is finite over $A$.

source.place: Setup before Tag 09IL; Algebra Tags 032W and 0331; componentwise finite normalization from N-2

proof.text:
Write $A^
u$ for the closure just constructed. Since $\pi_V$ is a nonzerodivisor, $Q(A)=Q(A_K)$. Every element of $A^
u$ is integral over $A_K$ after localization, hence lies in $A_K$ because a normal ring is integrally closed in its total fraction ring. Thus $A^
u$ is precisely the integral closure of $A$ inside $A_K$. The finite product decomposition of the Noetherian normal ring $A_K$ and the integral-closure normality lemma show that $A^
u$ is normal. It is Noetherian and finite type because it is finite over $A$. Its embedding in $A_K$ is torsion free over the PID $V$, hence flat. Finally $A\subseteq A^
u\subseteq A_K$ gives $A^
u[1/\pi_V]=A_K$. Apply this construction to $(V,A)=(D,E)$, and call the result $N$.

source.place: Setup before Tag 09IL; normality and generic identification of normalized base change

proof.text: Decompose the Noetherian normal ring $N=\prod_jN_j$ into finitely many normal domains. On each factor take all primes minimal over $(\pi)$; there are finitely many. Each such prime $\mathfrak p_i$ has height one: the principal ideal height bound gives height at most one, and $0\ne\pi\in\mathfrak p_i$ gives height at least one. Thus $T_i=(N_j)_{\mathfrak p_i}$ is a DVR by the one-dimensional normal-local criterion. The map $D\to T_i$ is injective and local, and $T_i$ is a localization at a prime of a finite type $D$-algebra. Apply the Epp input to obtain $F_i/F$.

source.place: Tag 09IL proof, vertical generic points and Tag 09II

proof.text: Let $R_i$ be the integral closure of $D$ in $F_i$. Each $R_i$ is a finite complete DVR by the complete-DVR normalization theorem. The common-extension theorem supplies one complete DVR $R$ finite over $D$ with compatible local embeddings $R_i\hookrightarrow R$. Put $L=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Then $L/F$ is finite and each $L/F_i$ is finite. The uniqueness clause of the complete-DVR normalization theorem identifies this $R$ with the integral closure of $D$ in $L$. If the family is empty take $R=D$ and $L=F$. The Epp conclusion holds for every $T_i$ with this $L$, because its statement allows every further finite extension.

source.place: Tag 09IL proof, common finite extension; Tag 0GLR

proof.text: Apply Steps 2–3 to $(V,A)=(R,E_R)$. For an injection of $R$-modules, its tensor with $E_R$ identifies with its tensor over $D$ with $E$; therefore $E_R$ is flat, it is finite type, and its generic fibre $E_F\otimes_F L$ is normal by the given geometric normality. The resulting finite normal flat algebra is exactly $C$ of the statement, with $C\otimes_RL=E_F\otimes_FL$. The integral algebra $N\otimes_D R$ embeds in that same generic ring and is integral over $E_R$. Transitivity of integrality shows that taking its integral closure gives the same $C$: an element integral over the larger algebra is integral over $E_R$, and a monic equation over $E_R$ is also one over the larger algebra. In particular $C$ is finite over $N$ as well, since $R/D$ and $C/E_R$ are finite.

source.place: Tag 09IL proof, normalized base change; generic normality is a hypothesis

proof.text: Fix a normal domain factor $C_b$ of $C$ and a height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ containing a uniformizer $\rho$ of $R$. Its map from $N$ factors through a domain factor $N_j$ and is injective on $N_j$: after inverting $\pi$, the minimal component of $E_F\otimes_FL$ dominates a component of $E_F$, since scalar extension is flat and a minimal prime contracts to a minimal prime by flat going down. Put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap N_j$. The extension $N_j\subset C_b$ is integral. Going down over the normal domain $N_j$ shows $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le1$. It contains $\pi$, since $\pi$ is a unit times a positive power of $\rho$ in $R$, so $\mathfrak p$ is one of the $\mathfrak p_i$ of Step 4.

source.place: Tag 09IL proof, locating the image of a vertical generic point; componentwise going down

proof.text: Localize $N\otimes_D R$ at $S=N_j\setminus\mathfrak p_i$, selecting the factor $N_j$. Its ring is $T_i\otimes_D R$. Integral closure commutes with this localization, so $S^{-1}C$ is its integral closure inside $H_i\otimes_F L$, where $H_i=\operatorname{Frac}(T_i)$: indeed $T_i[1/\pi]=H_i$. This generic tensor is reduced since it is a localization of the normal ring $E_F\otimes_FL$. Also $T_i\otimes_D R$ is integral over $T_i$, so transitivity identifies the closure with the ring $B_L$ in the Epp input. Localizing further at the image of $\mathfrak q$ identifies $C_{\mathfrak q}$ with $(B_L)_{\mathfrak q'}$. This is a maximal localization over the maximal ideal of $T_i$, since $B_L$ is integral over $T_i$. Epp now gives $\rho C_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q}$ and geometric reducedness over $k=R/(\rho)$ of the field $C_{\mathfrak q}/\rho C_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 09IL proof, omitted localization identification written out; Tags 0307, 09EM, 09E7

proof.text: For each domain factor $C_b$, every associated prime of $M_b=C_b/\rho C_b$ has height one by the normal principal-quotient lemma. Such primes are minimal over $(\rho)$, hence form a finite set. The associated-prime injection embeds $M_b$ into the finite product of its localizations at these primes. Step 8 identifies every factor with a field geometrically reduced over $k$. Tensor this injection over $k$ with an arbitrary field extension $\Omega/k$; fields are flat, so it remains injective. Tensor commutes with this finite product, whose resulting factors are reduced by Step 8. A nilpotent in $M_b\otimes_k\Omega$ therefore maps to zero in every factor and is zero. Taking the finite product over $b$ proves $(C/\rho C)\otimes_k\Omega$ reduced. Since $R$ is a DVR it has only one maximal ideal; this proves the last clause and finishes all assertions, including empty special fibres.
